items.title: POCSO case against father of minor cannot be settled by compromise with mother: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently held that a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) against a man accused of assaulting his own minor child cannot be dropped over a compromise arrived at between him and the child's mother [ Shiju v. State of Kerala & Ors. ]. Justice Kauser Edappagath held that any settlement entered into by a parent of a minor victim with the intention of ending criminal prosecution cannot be given legal sanction. Such settlements or compromises do not override the State's duty to prosecute offences against children, the Court said. “ The mother cannot legally settle or compromise a case against the father for sexual harassment or sexual assault of their minor daughter. Any compromise or out-of-court settlement effected by the parents of a minor victim with the object of stifling criminal prosecution cannot receive the sanction of law, nor can such a settlement override the State’s duty to prosecute offences against children. Courts, in the exercise of their parens patriae jurisdiction, bear a bounden duty to safeguard the rights of minor victims of sexual assault, even where parents fail to do so, ” the Court said in its order. The petition had been filed before the District Court at Chengalpattu under the Special Marriage Act, 1954, seeking divorce and maintenance alimony. Sangeetha had alleged the actor-turned-politician was involved in extra-marital relationship with an actress. However, she withdrew the petition on Friday. items.summary: Two men accused in the Renukaswamy murder case have moved applications before a Bengaluru sessions court seeking pardon under the law so that they can turn approvers and support the prosecution. The applications have been moved by Vinay V (accused no.10) and Pradosh S Rao @ Pradosh (accused no.14), both considered close associates of Kannada actor Darshan, the prime accused in the case. The applications were filed on August 5 before the Court of the 58th Additional City Civil and Sessions Court presided over by Judge Sujata Madivalappa Sambrani. The court has reserved its orders on the applicants' right of audience and posted the matter for orders on August 10, 2026. Sujata Madiwalappa Sambrani In their applications, the accused state that they are willing to make a "full and true disclosure" of all facts within their knowledge concerning the offence and the role of every person involved. They contend that their testimony would substantially assist the prosecution in establishing the case. In his application, Pradosh has claimed that he repeatedly tried to stop Darshan and others accused in the Renukaswamy murder case. 33-year-old Renukaswamy's dead body was found on June 9, 2024.

items.title: Bengaluru Police book Hindutva group over posts on Kunal Kamra show
items.summary: Bengaluru Police have registered a suo motu case against Mohan Gowda, State Organiser of the Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samithi, for allegedly spreading false and misleading information on social media regarding the cancellation of comedian Kunal Kamra's stand-up shows in the city. The FIR was registered by Whitefield Police based on a complaint filed by Police Constable Shridhar, who was on social media monitoring duty. According to the complaint, Gowda uploaded a video on his X account allegedly disseminating false and misleading information to the public about the comedian's performances. Police alleged that Gowda's videos and posts were intended to spread rumours and false information with the intention of causing harm. A case has been registered under Sections 217 and 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and further investigation is underway. The case comes days after the Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samithi submitted a memorandum to Bengaluru Police seeking the cancellation of Kamra's stand-up comedy shows in the city. items.title: DC review: Lokesh Kanagaraj tells a compelling tale in his acting debut
items.summary: DC (Tamil) Lokesh Kanagaraj has an undeniable talent for making you fond of on-screen gangsters. He could do it as a director. He pulls it off again in his acting debut. Arun Matheswaran’s DC stars Lokesh as Das, a ‘rowdie’ with a hair-trigger temper. Das and his gang race against time and police to pull off a heist of sorts. The film also makes attempts to question how criminality is often described without the socio-economic contexts that create it. Das’ full name is Devadas. While DC is said to be loosely based on the classic novel Devadas , it mostly tells its own story. Neither author Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay nor Sanjay Leela Bhansali, who adapted the novel for the screen in 2018, could have imagined a retelling of Devadas with such an abundance of shoot-outs, but here we are. The film declares its stance almost immediately after the opening credits. It shows how police brutality is wilfully targeted at the working class. What it could have dialled down is turning this violence into spectacle. Das is furious when he hears about the custodial murder of a poor farm worker. items.title: ‘He took loans to organise rescue missions’: Family of swimmer Rajesh who died in Kerala flood
items.summary: They were three siblings – Rajesh, Ranjith, and Asha – living with their parents and their many little dreams in a modest house in Kalliyoor, in the outskirts of Thiruvananthapuram. Two years ago, Ranjith passed away in a train mishap. Rajesh had then told his sister that they would be there for each other, a promise he could not keep for long. On August 4, Rajesh, a swimmer and rappelling instructor, was confirmed dead three days after he went missing during a rescue mission for the Kannur floods. He was 37. When his body was brought home, Asha felt a flurry of complaints brimming within her. This was a brother whom the family would hardly get to see; she had last met him a month ago when he came for Ranjith’s second death anniversary. The rest of the family – including Rajesh’s bereaved wife Safiya and two adolescent children – saw him a week ago before he rushed to the site of the disaster in Kannur.
